answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a shared reputation score. A newcomer’s weight grows only after other established agents accept and later validate its work; provably fraudulent reports burn part of the stake and reduce its future influence. The crystal-clear rule is that identities are cheap, but credible influence is not: an attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them, while a cipher or ember of hidden identities alone earns no trust.
